incidents.vector: Social-engineering and SIM-swap network intrusion carried out in the 2024 attack.
incidents.impact: Two leading members of the Scattered Spider collective were sentenced in the UK to 66 months for the 2024 TfL hack that halted network operations; one defendant was tied to 120+ attacks and $89.5M in traced crypto.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion detected July 16; initial entry vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Coca-Cola's Fairlife unit temporarily halted US production (plants in Michigan, New York and Arizona); scope still under investigation, product safety said to be unaffected and Canadian operations untouched.

incidents.vector: Fake CAPTCHA 'ClickFix' prompts on compromised sites trick victims into pasting PowerShell that installs GhettoVibe malware; also Signal and Android lures.
incidents.impact: Russian military intelligence shifted initial-access tactics against Ukrainian targets; CERT-UA observed ClickFix on 10+ compromised sites in June-July, with at least one infection leading to a destructive attack on a government network.

incidents.vector: Provided bulletproof hosting infrastructure and support that enabled malware, ransomware, phishing and brute-force attacks.
incidents.impact: Three Russian nationals behind Media Land and ML.Cloud were indicted for attacks causing over $62M in losses across 21 US states and several countries; a $10M State Department reward was offered for information.

incidents.vector: ClickFix social-engineering lures deliver ACR Stealer via WebDAV/Python loaders and a fileless MSHTA/PowerShell chain using steganography.
incidents.impact: Microsoft observed rising ACR Stealer (malware-as-a-service) activity harvesting browser credentials, authentication tokens and sensitive documents, with blockchain-backed dead-drop command-and-control.

incidents.victim: Software users in the US and Europe
incidents.vector: ClickFix lures push trojanized installers (MobaXterm, Webex, Zoom, DBeaver) deploying a Python 'Starland RAT' and bespoke PowerShell C2, then CastleStealer and Remcos.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos detailed campaign UAT-11795 stealing credentials and cryptocurrency wallets, with a Polygon smart contract used for fallback command-and-control resilience.

incidents.vector: Attackers chained two zero-days (CVE-2026-15409, CVE-2026-15410) for full appliance compromise; exploited from June 22, three weeks before the patch.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation of SMA1000 appliances (fewer than 5,000 units) with a likely ransomware objective per Rapid7; CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

incidents.vector: Intruders breached servers around July 13; the company disconnected key systems to contain the attack.
incidents.impact: Japan's largest cold-chain operator suffered an outage disrupting frozen and refrigerated deliveries to ~5,000 customers; KFC Japan's 1,300+ restaurants faced ingredient shortages, and some affected servers held personal data.

incidents.vector: Modular botnet brute-forces Telnet with ~1,500 credential pairs and carries exploits for 30+ IoT device families; LLM-assisted and cross-compiled for 17 architectures.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 detailed TuxBot v3, a DDoS-for-hire botnet with a Go-based command-and-control panel; developer infrastructure was traced to Iranian hosting.

incidents.vector: Elevation-of-privilege zero-days CVE-2026-56164 (on-prem SharePoint) and CVE-2026-56155 (Active Directory Federation Services) exploited in the wild.
incidents.impact: A record 622-CVE July Patch Tuesday included two actively exploited zero-days found by Microsoft's DART unit; a third SharePoint bug is the first half of an unauthenticated RCE chain.

incidents.vector: Attackers pushed malicious commits to unprotected AsyncAPI release branches, abusing GitHub Actions to harvest tokens and publish five trojanized npm packages carrying the Miasma RAT.
incidents.impact: Trojanized @asyncapi packages backdoor installs to steal GitHub/npm tokens, SSH keys, cloud credentials, Kubernetes tokens and CI/CD secrets.

incidents.victim: CISA (US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor published 844 MB of internal data — including AWS GovCloud credentials and plaintext usernames/passwords — to a public GitHub repo for roughly six months.
incidents.impact: Exposed admin credentials for dozens of internal systems; keys were rotated only after KrebsOnSecurity notified CISA, which says logs show no mission or customer data was accessed.

incidents.victim: UK Foreign Office (FCDO), embassies and local councils
incidents.vector: Firewall and VPN credentials harvested from ~80,000 Fortinet devices during the FortiBleed credential-theft campaign.
incidents.impact: A threat actor using the handle 'SantaAd' is selling a $60,000 archive of stolen FCDO, embassy and local-council firewall credentials.

incidents.victim: NetNut / Popa botnet (~2M consumer devices); operator Alarum Technologies
incidents.vector: Residential-proxy service populated the Popa botnet using at least two million devices compromised with little or no user consent, then rented for abusive traffic.
incidents.impact: The FBI and IRS-CI, with Google, Lumen and Shadowserver, seized hundreds of NetNut domains tied to mass scraping, ad fraud and account-takeover activity.

incidents.vector: Malicious on-chain governance attack.
incidents.impact: Attackers moved 4.4 trillion BONK (~$20M) to their own wallets; Upbit and Kraken paused BONK transactions during the investigation.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into a cloud platform, appearing tied to a broader Oracle PeopleSoft compromise campaign.
incidents.impact: An intruder accessed patient data and internal documents; the company disclosed the breach to the SEC after the hackers contacted it on June 15.

incidents.vector: Hacktivists gained broad network access and destroyed systems and backups.
incidents.impact: The Cyber Anarchy Squad claims it wiped 3,000 servers and workstations plus 700 VMs, deleted all backups, and stole over 650 TB of documents from the Russian construction firm.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion; entry vector undisclosed.
incidents.impact: The newly launched Settra ransomware group is extorting one of Taiwan's largest mobile operators; the telco says its mobile-payments platform was not impacted and the Ministry of Digital Affairs is investigating.

incidents.vector: Data breach under investigation; technical details not disclosed.
incidents.impact: A catastrophic data breach prompted South Korean authorities to levy a roughly $400M fine; the investigation remains active amid a US political dispute over the probe.

incidents.vector: Security breach during March-April; entry vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Kubota's North American division disclosed a breach that exposed employee information; no group has claimed responsibility.
